sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups, Princeton University Press 2008 (author's complete 600-page PDF)
sources.locator: Chapter 3, Sections 3.1-3.4 (printed pp. 26-43), Chapter 4, Sections 4.1-4.3 (printed pp. 44-48), and Example 6.7.1 (printed pp. 92-93); the named lemmas, propositions and theorems were read in the extracted full text, figures were used only as illustrations

contents.name: Section 3.1: dihedral groups, the normal forms 1_k, 2_k and the product st
Lemma 3.2.6: if r_i = r_j then the two letters can be deleted
Lemma 3.2.14: a word is reduced if and only if its prefix reflections are distinct
Conditions (D) deletion, (E) exchange, (F) folding, and Theorem 3.2.16 (equivalence)
Lemma 3.3.5: the action U_s(eps,r) = (eps (-1)^{delta(s,r)}, srs) and expression-independence of the sign count
Theorem 3.3.4: Coxeter system iff Cayley graph is a reflection system iff Exchange Condition
Definition 3.4.1: elementary M-operations and M-reduced words
Theorem 3.4.2 (Tits): reduced expressions are exactly M-reduced, and braid moves connect any two reduced expressions
Proposition 4.1.1, Corollaries 4.1.2-4.1.5 and Theorem 4.1.6: support, special subgroups and agreement of intrinsic and ambient length
Lemma 4.2.2: r lies in R(1,w) if and only if l(rw) < l(w)
contents.reason: The reflection/half-space separation formalism is not used on this pair: the sign-change set is developed from the algebraic signed action and the inversion count instead, with no reflection-wall or Cayley-graph geometry.

contents.name: Lemma 4.3.1 and Lemma 4.3.3: the shortest element in a special coset, unique factorization and length additivity
Example 6.7.1: the symmetric group is the Coxeter group of type A_{n-1}
Section 3.5 and Sections 6.1-6.12: Coxeter diagrams, geometric reflection groups, finite and affine classification
contents.reason: The diagram classification of finite Coxeter groups is the subject of the Coxeter-groups track page of this run; the present pair uses only the type-A matrix and does not claim any classification.

sources.title: George Lusztig, Hecke Algebras with Unequal Parameters (revised 2014 book text, arXiv:math/0208154v2, 141 pp.)
sources.locator: Chapter 1, Sections 1.1-1.11 (printed pp. 10-19), and Chapter 9, Sections 9.1-9.7 (printed pp. 39-41); every proof in those ranges was read in the extracted full text

contents.name: 1.1-1.2 and Lemma 1.2: the Coxeter matrix, the presented group, the sign character, length, and l(sw) = l(w) +/- 1
Proposition 1.3: the maps sigma_s(e_{s'}) = e_{s'} + 2cos(pi/m_{s,s'}) e_s, and ss' has order exactly m_{s,s'}
Corollary 1.4: the dihedral subgroup consists of 1_k and 2_k, distinct except at the ends, with l(1_k) = l(2_k) = k
Proposition 1.5: the action U_s on {1,-1} x T and the even 2m-term sign count
Proposition 1.6: the inversion subset of a reduced word is independent of the reduced expression
Proposition 1.7: exchange (l(sw) = l(w) - 1 gives ss_1...s_{j-1} = s_1...s_j)
1.8 and Theorem 1.9 (Matsumoto/Tits): braid moves connect any two reduced expressions
Proposition 1.10: the folding statement l(swt) = l(w), l(sw) = l(wt) implies sw = wt
contents.reason: The folding assertion is proved locally from exchange in lem-hh-commuting-left-right-hecke-length-operators, Proof 1.3, and consumed there in 2.1. HH-11 supplies exchange, not a separate folding item; its proof home in this approved run is HH-12.

contents.name: 1.11: the symmetric bilinear form (e_s,e_{s'}) = -cos(pi/m) and the notion of tame W
contents.reason: Bilinear forms, tameness and the finite/non-integral classification are not needed here; the geometric representation is used only through its relators and its action on the quotient by a rank-two plane.

contents.name: Lemma 9.1: any word can be reduced to a subsequence that is a reduced expression
9.2-9.3: the support S_w and W_I = {w : S_w subset I}
9.4-9.6, Proposition 9.5: the intrinsic presentation W*_I -> W_I is an isomorphism, and l_I = l
Lemma 9.7: unique minimal coset element, descent characterisation and l(yw) = l(y) + l(w)
Lemma 9.8 and 9.11-9.16: maximal coset elements, double cosets and Hecke-theoretic refinements
contents.reason: Longest elements, double cosets and the Hecke-theoretic cell refinements are not claimed on this page; the one-sided minimal coset theory is the endpoint of the pair.

sources.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups, Springer GTM 231 (2005) (complete author/class-hosted 370-page PDF)
sources.locator: Section 1.5 (printed pp. 18-22), including Theorem 1.5.1 and Propositions 1.5.2-1.5.4, the Deletion Property Proposition 1.4.7 referenced by that proof, and Proposition 2.4.4 with Corollary 2.4.5 (printed pp. 39-40)

contents.name: The Exchange Property and the Deletion Property for a group with a generating set of involutions
Theorem 1.5.1: Coxeter system iff Exchange Property iff Deletion Property, with the proof that every relation follows from the pairwise relations
Proposition 1.4.7: the Deletion Property, referenced in the proof of Theorem 1.5.1
Proposition 1.5.2: the length of a permutation with respect to adjacent transpositions equals its inversion number
Proposition 1.5.3: the right descent set of a permutation is its set of descents
Proposition 1.5.4: (S_n, S) is a Coxeter system of type A_{n-1}, proved by the Exchange Property
Proposition 2.4.4 and Corollary 2.4.5: parabolic factorization W = W^J W_J with l(w) = l(w^J) + l(w_J) and unique minimal coset representatives
Corollary 2.4.6: the iterated product map Q_1 x ... x Q_n -> W is a bijection with additive length
contents.reason: The iterated maximal-parabolic normal form is not claimed on this pair; only one standard parabolic at a time, together with its cosets, is treated in the scaffolded items.
